title: The Best Umbreon Cards to Collect — Neo Discovery to Moonbreon and Umbreon ex, Raw to PSA 10, Dated Sold Prices | Gengar's Collector's Desk
description: Gengar's pick of the Umbreon cards that are true collectibles: Neo Discovery Umbreon (1st Edition and Unlimited), the Skyridge and Aquapolis holos, the Evolving Skies Umbreon VMAX alternate art (Moonbreon), the Prismatic Evolutions Umbreon ex, the Hidden Fates shiny and an under-$30 shelf — each with dated raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 sold prices and eBay links.
keywords: best umbreon cards, umbreon cards to collect, moonbreon, umbreon vmax alt art, umbreon ex prismatic evolutions, neo discovery umbreon, most valuable umbreon cards, umbreon card collection
intro: Umbreon is the quiet one. No fire, no legend, just a black Eeveelution with gold rings that has somehow produced the most-chased modern English card of its era and three of the hardest vintage holos to find in a 10. These are the ones that belong in a collection.
narratorNote: A dark type and a ghost type get along fine. Two of the Umbreons below already have full price pages on this site — Moonbreon and the Prismatic Umbreon ex — so this desk links to them instead of repeating them. Every number is a dated sold price from our own index data, and nothing here is a call to buy or sell.

shelves.label: The grails
shelves.blurb: Three Wizards-era Umbreon holos from the last two years of the WOTC run. Dark cards, tiny print runs, and PSA 10 prices to match.

entries.title: Neo Discovery Umbreon #13 (2001)
entries.why: Umbreon's first card, a holo from Neo Discovery. It is the heaviest card in both our Neo Discovery indices, and the 1st Edition PSA 10 is one of the biggest numbers on this site. The #32 non-holo is the same set's affordable Umbreon.

entries.title: Skyridge Umbreon H30 and #32 (2003)
entries.why: Skyridge's Umbreon holo is one of the rarest Umbreons in a 10 — it trades almost only graded, which is why there is no clean raw mark on it. The #32 is the non-holo rare from the same single-print-run set.

entries.title: Aquapolis Umbreon H29 and #41 (2003)
entries.why: The Aquapolis holo is the second of the e-Card Umbreons and the one of the heaviest cards in our Aquapolis index. The #41 is its non-holo twin.

shelves.label: The centerpieces
shelves.blurb: The modern Umbreons — including the one that defines the modern market.

entries.title: Umbreon VMAX alternate art #215, Evolving Skies (2021)
entries.why: The alternate-art Umbreon VMAX from Evolving Skies is the most-chased English card of the Sword & Shield era and the heaviest card in our Evolving Skies index by a wide margin. It has its own price page here — how much is Moonbreon worth — with the full print list. The rainbow #214 and the regular #95 are the same card in the other frames.

entries.title: Umbreon V alternate art #189, Evolving Skies (2021)
entries.why: The alternate-art Umbreon V from the same set, the card most collectors pair with Moonbreon. The #188 full art and the #94 regular are the budget frames.

entries.title: Umbreon ex #161, Prismatic Evolutions (2025)
entries.why: The Special Illustration Rare from Prismatic Evolutions, the heaviest card in that index and the Scarlet & Violet era's answer to Moonbreon. It has its own price page too — how much is Umbreon ex worth.

entries.title: Umbreon GX SV69, Hidden Fates (2019)
entries.why: The shiny Umbreon GX from the Hidden Fates Shiny Vault, one of the heaviest cards in our Hidden Fates index, right behind the Charizard GX. The shiny Umbreon's blue rings are the whole point.

entries.title: Umbreon #17, Celebrations (2021)
entries.why: The Celebrations main-set Umbreon, one of the heaviest cards in that index. A clean, cheap holo for a collector building the Eeveelution run.

entries.title: Umbreon V #94, Evolving Skies (2021)
entries.why: The regular Umbreon V from Evolving Skies. Same set as Moonbreon, same year, a few dollars.

entries.title: Umbreon ex #92 and Umbreon #91, 30th Celebration (2026)
entries.why: This year's Umbreons from the 30th Celebration main set, the ex and the regular. Too new for graded marks; a couple of dollars raw.

collectingNotes.h: Three vintage holos, all hard grades
collectingNotes.p: Neo Discovery, Aquapolis and Skyridge each printed an Umbreon holo, and all three are dark cards from the end of the Wizards run with small print runs. Two of them trade almost only graded, which is why their raw column is thin or empty.

collectingNotes.h: 1st Edition and Unlimited are different cards
collectingNotes.p: Neo Discovery exists as a 1st Edition print and an Unlimited print with separate PSA labels, separate population reports and separate price histories. Our indices track them separately and every link here searches for the exact print on the row.

collectingNotes.h: Two Umbreons with their own pages
collectingNotes.p: Moonbreon and the Prismatic Umbreon ex each have a full price page on this site with every print of that card. This desk links to them rather than repeating them; the ladders here are the same index data.

PSA 10 is the hobby's price reference. TAG grades by machine-measured imaging with human review and publishes a full defect report for every card, which is why we link TAG slabs beside PSA on every row. We think measured grading is where the hobby is heading — our view, not a price claim. How TAG grading works →
